title: Chat parser resilience and bundle handshake for model onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We have observed intermittent failures and subtle content drift when new model bundles are onboarded to the runtime. Failures are concentrated around message framing differences (role markers, delimiter variants, and sparse whitespace) and mismatches between the model bundle's tokenization behavior and the onboarding templates used by the Console. This ticket implements a two-part approach: (1) a resilient chat-parsing layer that tolerates minor delimiter/marker variants and normalizes framed messages with minimal change to token counts, and (2) a lightweight handshake schema to be embedded in model bundles that declares preferred delimiters, role tokens, and tokenizer fingerprint metadata so the onboarding pipeline can publish an accurate performance profile and avoid incorrect pinning decisions.

Scope / Goals:
- Add a parsing pass that normalizes message boundaries while preserving token alignment for the runtime's cache and batching logic.
- Define and validate a bundle handshake JSON that bundles must include (fields: tokenizer_hash, preferred_delimiters, role_marker_variants, recommended_chat_template, subtoken_shift_estimate).
- Update onboarding validation to compute a token-shift metric and gate profile publishing if shift > threshold.
- Emit telemetry for "subtoken_shift_rate", "framing_reflow_count", and "bundle_handshake_mismatch" to Console dashboards.

Out of scope:
- Changes to public SDK chat templates (handled by product).
- Full tokenizer re-training or model changes.

Why this matters:
Incorrect assumptions about framing/tokenization lead to bad profile publishes (wrong latency/cost numbers), unexpected model regressions when pinned, and customer-facing anomalies for chat features. A small defensive handshake combined with a tolerant parser reduces onboarding toil and prevents many customer incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime includes a parsing normalization pass that handles at least three delimiter variants and soft role markers without changing message semantics.
Model bundles that include a handshake JSON are validated during onboarding; mismatches produce a clear warning and a gated stop for profile publish.
Onboarding pipeline computes subtoken_shift_rate and blocks publish when rate > 2.5% for canonical eval prompts (configurable).
Telemetry emitted and visible in Console: subtoken_shift_rate, framing_reflow_count, bundle_handshake_mismatch.
Unit and integration tests cover edgecases: leading/trailing whitespace, escaped role tokens, token boundary splits across KV-cache chunks.
comments: 2025-02-24 Aisha Patel: Initial triage. Reproduced a case where a Llama-derived bundle uses '>>' as speaker marker and onboarding templates use '\n\n' boundaries; caused +4% token shift in short chats. Logging sample attached.

2025-02-26 Jared Kim: Spike implemented a PoC parser that normalizes role markers to a canonical '\u0001role:' token before tokenization. Early results: token shift down from 4% to 0.9% on our sample suite. Needs broader test coverage and perf measurement.

2025-02-28 Marco Huang (review): Reviewed PoC. Two concerns: (1) preserve exact byte offsets for KV cache to avoid invalid cache keys; (2) handshake schema must be tolerant to missing fields for older bundles. Suggested adding 'compat_level' with default 'v0'.
2025-03-01 Aisha Patel: Implemented handshake schema draft and onboarding validation. Added metric 'subtoken_shift_rate' and a threshold gate set to 2.5% by default. Created draft PR.

2025-03-03 Code review (PR feedback): Addressed Marco's KV offset concern by performing normalization after computing canonical KV key offsets; added fuzz tests for escaped role markers. Also added clear telemetry tags: bundle_id, model_name, onboarding_run_id.
2025-03-04 Jared Kim: Moving to 'In Progress' to finalize tests, update docs, and land runtime PR. QA plan scheduled for 2025-03-06.
